topic.title: Few-Shot and Zero-Shot Generalization
topic.overview: Few-shot learning adapts from very small labeled datasets, while zero-shot learning relies on transferable semantic information for unseen categories. This topic includes synthetic augmentation, cross-domain transfer, vision-language adaptation, and calibration between seen and unseen classes. One representative method tunes a language model to generate label-discriminative training examples, then uses them to augment scarce supervision.
topic.whyItMatters: Limited labels make models sensitive to sampling noise, domain mismatch, and biases inherited from pretraining. Additional generated data or semantic prototypes help only when they preserve the distinctions needed by the new task.
topic.evolution: The representatives begin with semantic output codes and compositional one-shot learning. Later work examines dataset generalization, unlabeled target data, and online adapters. Recent papers analyze synthetic-data benefits, noisy few-shot settings, and methods for correcting seen-class bias during generalized zero-shot inference.
openQuestions: When does synthetic augmentation add information instead of reinforcing initial errors?
How can unseen-class calibration be evaluated without exploiting unavailable test labels?

papers.title: Conjugated Semantic Pool Improves OOD Detection with Pre-trained Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: Modified broad-category descriptions improve zero-shot unfamiliar-image detection by expanding label candidates in a theoretically motivated way.

papers.title: D2R2: Diffusion-based Representation with Random Distance Matching for Tabular Few-shot Learning
papers.tldr: D2R2 combines diffusion representations, distance preservation, and iterative prototypes to improve tabular classification with few labeled examples.

papers.title: Dual Risk Minimization: Towards Next-Level Robustness in Fine-tuning Zero-Shot Models
papers.tldr: DRM uses language-generated core-feature descriptions to balance ordinary training performance with estimated worst-case risk during fine-tuning.

papers.title: FAST: A Dual-tier Few-Shot Learning Paradigm for Whole Slide Image Classification
papers.tldr: FAST combines patch retrieval and vision-language prompts to approach fully supervised slide classification accuracy with very little annotation.

papers.title: Generate Universal Adversarial Perturbations for Few-Shot Learning
papers.tldr: FSAFW improves universal adversarial perturbation transfer in few-shot learning by addressing both task and semantic shifts.

papers.title: Interpreting and Analysing CLIP's Zero-Shot Image Classification via Mutual Knowledge
papers.tldr: The paper explains CLIP's zero-shot classifications through textual concepts shared by its image and language encoders.

papers.title: Meta-Exploiting Frequency Prior for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning
papers.tldr: Frequency-based feature and prediction consistency improve cross-domain few-shot learning without adding inference-time computation.

papers.title: Mind the Gap Between Prototypes and Images in Cross-domain Finetuning
papers.tldr: CoPA improves cross-domain few-shot classification by adapting class prototypes and image embeddings with separate transformations.

papers.title: Mixture of Adversarial LoRAs: Boosting Robust Generalization in Meta-Tuning
papers.tldr: AMT trains a pool of adversarially perturbed LoRA adapters and dynamically merges them to improve out-of-domain few-shot classification.

papers.title: No "Zero-Shot" Without Exponential Data: Pretraining Concept Frequency Determines Multimodal Model Performance
papers.tldr: Across tested multimodal models, zero-shot performance strongly tracks pretraining concept frequency, with linear gains requiring exponentially more data.

papers.title: OTTER: Effortless Label Distribution Adaptation of Zero-shot Models
papers.tldr: OTTER uses optimal transport and an estimated downstream label distribution to improve zero-shot classification predictions.

papers.title: Revisiting Few-Shot Object Detection with Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: Foundational FSOD reframes few-shot detection as adapting pretrained vision-language models to application-specific concepts using text and visual examples.

papers.title: TPR: Topology-Preserving Reservoirs for Generalized Zero-Shot Learning
papers.tldr: TPR combines an attribute reservoir with preserved class geometry to improve recognition of mixed seen and unseen classes.

papers.title: A Generalization Theory for Zero-Shot Prediction
papers.tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework identifying what zero-shot prediction learns and the conditional independence relationships that enable generalization.

papers.title: Addressing Imbalanced Domain-Incremental Learning through Dual-Balance Collaborative Experts
papers.tldr: DCE combines frequency-specialized experts with a learned selector to handle class imbalance as domains change.

papers.title: Does One-shot Give the Best Shot? Mitigating Model Inconsistency in One-shot Federated Learning
papers.tldr: FAFI improves one-shot federated learning by aligning client representations before combining their features and category prototypes.

papers.title: Few-Shot Learner Generalizes Across AI-Generated Image Detection
papers.tldr: FSD learns a metric space that supports detection of images from unseen generators using very few additional samples.

papers.title: Foundation Model Insights and a Multi-Model Approach for Superior Fine-Grained One-shot Subset Selection
papers.tldr: RAM-APL combines complementary foundation models to improve one-shot subset selection for fine-grained image datasets.

papers.title: GenZSL: Generative Zero-Shot Learning Via Inductive Variational Autoencoder
papers.tldr: GenZSL generates unseen-class features from similar seen classes and class-name embeddings, improving benchmark performance and training efficiency.

papers.title: Provably Improving Generalization of Few-shot models with Synthetic Data
papers.tldr: A theory-guided prototype-learning method improves few-shot classification by addressing distribution differences between real and synthetic data.

papers.title: Random Registers for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning
papers.tldr: Random register tokens perturb vision-transformer attention and improve cross-domain few-shot transfer in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Revisiting Continuity of Image Tokens for Cross-domain Few-shot Learning
papers.tldr: Disrupting continuity between image patches encourages smaller-scale visual patterns and improves few-shot transfer across large domain gaps.

papers.title: Self-Disentanglement and Re-Composition for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation
papers.tldr: Learning weights for vision Transformer component comparisons reduces feature entanglement and improves cross-domain few-shot segmentation.

papers.title: Diffusion-Classifier Synergy: Reward-Aligned Learning via Mutual Boosting Loop for FSCIL
papers.tldr: DCS couples a diffusion generator and incremental classifier in a reward-guided feedback loop that improves old-class retention and new-class learning.

papers.title: Domain-RAG: Retrieval-Guided Compositional Image Generation for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Object Detection
papers.tldr: Domain-RAG preserves foreground objects and generates retrieval-guided backgrounds to improve few-shot detection across visual domains.

papers.title: Dual Alignment Framework for Few-shot Learning with Inter-Set and Intra-Set Shifts
papers.tldr: DUAL combines feature repair and two-stage distribution alignment to improve few-shot classification under shifts within and between example sets.

papers.title: Enhancing Zero-Shot Black-Box Optimization via Pretrained Models with Efficient Population Modeling, Interaction, and Stable Gradient Approximation
papers.tldr: EPOM improves pretrained black-box optimizers through richer task features, more flexible strategies, and differentiable training operations.

papers.title: Evolving and Regularizing Meta-Environment Learner for Fine-Grained Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning
papers.tldr: Meta-Environment Learner improves fine-grained incremental classification by evolving shared features while regularizing model complexity.

papers.title: Filter Like You Test: Data-Driven Data Filtering for CLIP Pretraining
papers.tldr: FLYT learns which pretraining examples help downstream tasks and samples them with repetition control, improving reported CLIP benchmark performance.

papers.title: Graph Few-Shot Learning via Adaptive Spectrum Experts and Cross-Set Distribution Calibration
papers.tldr: GRACE improves graph few-shot learning by adapting spectral processing locally and calibrating differences between support and query distributions.

papers.title: MAPLE: Multi-scale Attribute-enhanced Prompt Learning for Few-shot Whole Slide Image Classification
papers.tldr: MAPLE combines prompts for histological structures and whole slides with cross-scale graph learning to improve few-shot pathology classification.

papers.title: Preference-driven Knowledge Distillation for Few-shot Node Classification
papers.tldr: Preference-driven distillation transfers language-model knowledge through multiple graph teachers, selecting suitable supervision for each node before training a student.

papers.title: TOMCAT: Test-time Comprehensive Knowledge Accumulation for Compositional Zero-Shot Learning
papers.tldr: TOMCAT updates aligned text and image prototypes from unlabeled test data to improve recognition of unseen attribute-object combinations.

papers.title: Weak-shot Keypoint Estimation via Keyness and Correspondence Transfer
papers.tldr: Transferring local keypoint preferences and cross-image correspondences enables keypoint learning for unlabeled novel classes using labeled base classes.

papers.title: Bayes-inspired Integration of Pretrained Priors and Few-Shot Evidence for Few-Shot Classification
papers.tldr: BOIF separates pretrained knowledge from few-shot evidence and combines their scores using a Bayesian-inspired rule.

papers.title: Granularity-Aware Adaptive Classifier Expansion via Zero-Shot Learning
papers.tldr: A granularity-aware framework expands classifiers from class semantics by separating broad distinctions, refining similar classes, and suppressing non-causal noise.

papers.title: Improving CLIP Adaptation by Breaking Tail Alignment for Source-Free Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning
papers.tldr: ATHA improves few-shot CLIP adaptation by selectively strengthening useful image-text alignment and weakening alignment for low-similarity tokens.

papers.title: Minimizing Mismatch Risk: A Prototype-Based Routing Framework for Zero-shot LLM-generated Text Detection
papers.tldr: DetectRouter improves zero-shot generated-text detection by selecting a surrogate model suited to each input.

papers.title: OOVDet: Low-Density Prior Learning for Zero-Shot Out-of-Vocabulary Object Detection
papers.tldr: OOVDet learns to reject undefined objects using synthesized unknown prompts and uncertain images, guided by a low-density latent-space assumption.

papers.title: Rank-guided Diffusion for Noise Few-Shot Learning
papers.tldr: The method detects noisy few-shot examples through rank anomalies and uses constrained diffusion to replace them with more consistent samples.

papers.title: When Generalized Zero-Shot Learning Meets PU Learning: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Seen-Class Bias Mitigation
papers.tldr: PUFE reduces seen-class bias in generalized zero-shot learning through positive-unlabeled classification and adaptive semantic-prototype calibration.
